learning: Iteration 3 showed that lead 0.04 m hurts all tracks, so lead 0.06 m is kept. Slalom line loss persisted at both leads and with the 16 mm footprint, so the next test is turn authority through wheel_track.
notes: Runnable package: the Builder's restored 12 mm, 0.06 m lead, +/-0.03 m geometry with wheel_track 0.10 m. The controller is identical to the iteration 1 design, so the wheel_track change is the only variable under test.
rationale: Iteration 1 is the best-measured design (score 631.8). Its 12 mm footprints, 0.06 m lead and +/-0.03 m span gave the s-bend 16/20 finishes, and the oval finished 20/20 at 1.84 s. Iteration 3 showed that the 0.04 m lead hurts every track, and iteration 2 showed that the 16 mm footprint gives no slalom benefit. The Builder's geometry restores that sensing and narrows wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a 0.10 m track gives about 20% more turn per unit of turn command, which is the authority the slalom needs. The controller therefore stays exactly as it raced in iteration 1 (kp 3.0, kd 0.75, ki 0, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, linear weights -2 to +2). Keeping kp fixed isolates the wheel_track effect, and the oval's time margin (1.84 s against a 3 s limit) absorbs any loss of straight-line speed. The main risk is higher effective gain on the s-bend, where steering_oscillation is already 0.33 to 0.34, so the next race reports steering_oscillation on all three tracks. No result is claimed for this package.
